prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Yes We Can—win the best for Scotland. The SNP’s 1997 manifesto sets out a confident, costed route to independence so Scotland can put its wealth to work for jobs, public services and social justice.

Why independence
- Scotland is wealthy and pays her way; Treasury figures show Scotland has sent billions more to London than received. Small nations thrive; so can we.
- Myths debunked: automatic EU membership; open border with England; pensions/investments protected; inclusive citizenship by birth or residence; modern, non-nuclear defence.
- Only independence lets Scotland speak for itself, invest its surplus at home, and choose any government it wants under proportional representation.

How to gain it
- Elect a majority of SNP MPs; open negotiations with the UK and EU; present the independence settlement to a simple referendum; on approval, declare independence and hold fresh elections.

A democratic Scotland for all her people
- Written constitution and Bill of Rights, protecting civil, social and economic rights (housing, education, health, decent work, minimum wage).
- Single-chamber PR parliament, votes from 16+, public petitions, powerful committees; reform the monarchy; entrench strong, PR-elected local government.

Working in a better Scotland
- Aim for full employment; 100,000 extra jobs; national apprenticeships; export and skills agencies; R&D and tourism boosts.
- Competitive business taxes: cut corporation tax (main to 30p; small to 18p); abolish Class IV NICs; fair, banded business rates.
- Fair personal taxes: introduce a 15p starter rate; widen basic band; remove NI ceiling; cut VAT on fuel to 5%. Adopt the Social Chapter and a consensus minimum wage; guarantee trade union rights.

Living in a better Scotland
- Social justice: raise Child Benefit; restore benefits for 16–17s; increase pensions; introduce a Cold Climate Allowance; remove utility standing charges for pensioners; end means testing for residential care.
- Rebuild a true NHS: abolish the internal market; cut bureaucracy; add funds; reintegrate dentistry; strengthen prevention (ban tobacco ads, raise duty) and food safety (independent agency).
- Safer communities: “zero tolerance” of everyday crime; smarter sentencing and rehabilitation; ban handguns and implement Cullen.

Serving communities
- Education: hire 700 teachers; repair schools; guaranteed internet in every school; free nursery for 3–4s; restore student grants; expand training.
- Housing: transfer 75% of council housing debt to central government; build new homes; renovate substandard stock; protect new/improved social homes from discounted right-to-buy.
- Reform local services: abolish water quangos; invigorate arts, film and broadcasting with a Scottish Broadcasting Corporation; support Gaelic and Scots; launch a fairer “Scot-Lot” lottery.

Helping all of Scotland
- Land reform: abolish feudal tenure; transparent land register; local control of shore/seabed.
- Back farming (CAP reform, traceability), fisheries (regional management, processing support), forestry (double woodland cover), crofting development.
- Environment: empower SEPA; set national targets; end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay and build a renewables R&D centre.
- Energy: secure Scotland’s North Sea share; fair gas access; phase out nuclear; expand renewables and efficiency.
- Transport: public ownership of Scottish Railtrack assets; rail electrification; end bridge tolls (Skye first); strengthen ferries; fairer air duty for the Highlands and Islands.
- Telecoms: rural connectivity, distance learning leadership, pro‑innovation internet policy.

Europe and the world
- Be a full EU member with vote and veto; more MEPs; Scottish Commissioner and presidency turns.
- Targeted embassies; join UN, Commonwealth, Council of Europe; co‑operate across the British Isles.
- Defence: professional conventional forces; remove Trident; withdraw from NATO’s nuclear structures while co‑operating via European and partnership frameworks; defence diversification; peacekeeping college.
- Aid: grow to 0.7% of GDP in six years.

Paying for it
- A fully costed four‑year budget invests in people and services, reallocates from Trident, leverages Scotland’s fiscal surplus, and repays £6.6bn of debt.

Yes We Can—and if the SNP wins, so does Scotland.
